newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran vows its pilgrims will hold rally at haj.
newsitem.headline: Iran vows its pilgrims will hold rally at haj.

text.p: Iran's top official at the Moslem haj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia vowed on Friday that Iranian pilgrims would hold a rally to denounce the United States and Israel next week despite a Saudi ban.

Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahri told the Iranian news agency IRNA in Mecca that the "disavowal of infidels" rally would be held on Monday "with all its splendor due to the current sensitive circumstances that Moslem nations are facing."
He said the rally would be held in the holy city of Mecca or in nearby Mena or Mount Arafat "based on circumstances for Iranian haj pilgrims", the agency said.

Saudi authorities have banned all political activities during the haj. On Wednesday the kingdom urged Iranian pilgrims to refrain from holding the rally which has been an issue straining ties between the two Gulf powers for years.
The haj reaches its climax next week.

Radical Shi'ite Iran says Moslems should air their political grievances during the haj, mainly through rallies to denounce Israel and the United States as enemies of Islam. Conservative Sunni Saudi Arabia says the pilgrimage is purely religious and should not be politicised.

The row between the Gulf's two richest oil states over the rallies has resurfaced at every haj since 1987, when 402 people, mostly Iranians, died in clashes with Saudi security forces at an Iranian-led rally. Iran boycotted the haj for three years.
Saudi Arabia has said it would deal harshly with violators of the ban on political activity during haj.
To avoid confrontation with Saudi security, Iranian pilgrims in recent years staged low-key rallies within Iran's haj compounds and Saudi forces did not interfere.
About two million Moslems -- half of them from outside Saudi Arabia -- are expected to perform this year's haj at Mecca, site of Islam's holiest shrine.
